chunk_findings.detail: In fish, `set -l _out (register-python-argcomplete --shell fish ddflow 2>/dev/null)` stores each line of the command’s stdout as a separate list element; quoting `$_out` does not turn that list into a single multi-line string. In the comment case `source` returns 0 while registering nothing; in the syntax-error case the error is sent to `/dev/null` and `or return 0` makes the activation function return 0 anyway. Thus sourcing the fish activation can silently produce no completion even though `register-python-argcomplete` succeeded, whereas the previous direct `register-python-argcomplete ... | source` preserved the script verbatim.
